chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from a man, from Yahya ibn Ubada, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A wet twig of the length of a cubit is taken and placed, and he gestured with his hand from his collarbone to his hand, [saying it is] wrapped with his garment.
He said, And the man said, I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) afterwards and asked him about it, so he said: Yes, I had narrated it to Yahya ibn Ubada.

key_terms.جَرِيدَةٌ: A fresh palm branch or twig

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual significance of placing a wet twig on the deceased's chest in Shia burial practices?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* details the specific Sunnah of placing a fresh palm twig (*jarid*) on the chest of the deceased during shrouding, a practice rooted in the teachings of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). The verification by Yahya ibn Ubada underscores the reliability of this transmission within Shia jurisprudence, linking the physical act to spiritual symbolism. The use of a 'wet' twig likely signifies freshness and vitality, serving as a tangible reminder of resurrection and the continuity of life beyond death.
